title: Pete Capitán (Chas McIvor)
style: country blues acoustic guitar warm baritone male vocal storytelling 104bpm walking bass brushed drums honest eldest son family portrait Australian character unhurried
lyrics:
[Intro - acoustic guitar, steady and wide]
Peter John McIvor.
The oldest one.
Chas has him in the phone as Pete Capitán.
That tells you everything
You need to know.

[Verse 1]
He came first
Before Corey
Before Joel
Seven years before Corey
Gave the family its shape
The eldest always does
Before you know what shape means
Pete was already there
Setting the register
For how McIvor men carry themselves

[Verse 2]
He played rugby
Because Dad played rugby
And the son plays what the father plays
When the father is Chas McIvor
And the son is Pete
And the game is real
And the field is honest
And the thing underneath is always:
We do this properly
Or we don't do it at all

[Chorus]
Pete Capitán
That's what Dad put in the phone
Pete Capitán
The oldest one
Pete Capitán
November twenty-sixth
Every year
The text comes at one in the morning
Pete Capitán
Call Pete
Double exclamation
Pete Capitán
Dad doesn't miss it
Pete Capitán
He never has

[Bridge - spoken, Chas voice, level and proud]
"Call Pete!!" He texted that.
To his middle son.
About his oldest son.
Because Pete needed to be called
And Corey hadn't called yet
And Chas knew
And reminded him.
That's how it works in this family.
Dad keeps the calendar.
Dad makes the calls.
And when the call needs making
And someone hasn't made it
Dad says: Call Pete.
Double exclamation.
Pete Capitán.

[Verse 3]
Seven years older than Corey
Which means he was a man
When his brother was still a kid
And he carried that
The way the oldest carries it
Which is usually quietly
And almost always completely

[Chorus reprise]
Pete Capitán
Oldest son
Pete Capitán
Rugby in the blood
Pete Capitán
November twenty-sixth
Every year
Without fail
Pete Capitán
That's my boy

[Outro - guitar alone, settled]
The Capitán
Was here first
Set the standard
Kept the register
And Chas put it in the phone
Pete Capitán
Which is how you know
Dad always knew
What Pete was
From the beginning
